purpose: Combine the frozen Stage A and Stage B outputs into one General Draft Board and one Overall Score /100.

frozen_stage_b.normalization_note: STANDARD, not SEASON_RELATIVE. The +0.0031 macro Spearman from switching is NOT sufficient to reopen Stage B (DEC-095).

holdout_policy: 2026 is never loaded, scored, ranked or used to choose any formula or scaling constant.

stage_b_applied_to_all_prospects.interpretation: If this basketball profile were draftable, where would it resemble the drafted population? It is NOT a claim that the prospect will be drafted, and NOT a pick assignment.
stage_b_applied_to_all_prospects.target_unchanged: An undrafted prospect keeps drafted=0 and pick=NULL. No synthetic pick is ever created.
stage_b_applied_to_all_prospects.audit_required: Report the prediction distribution separately for historically drafted and undrafted validation prospects.

stage_b_transforms.formula: percentile rank of stage_b quality (= -predicted pick) among that validation year's board
stage_b_transforms.why_tested: Purely relative to the board being ranked, so it needs no draft-size constant and no clipping. The natural partner for a rank-fusion rule.

stage_b_transforms.clipping: PREDECLARED to the basketball-valid slot range [1, draft_size]. Measured on development OOF: 1 of 617 predictions falls below 1 and 0 above draft size, so clipping touches 0.16% of rows.
stage_b_transforms.why_tested: Keeps an absolute draft-slot meaning, so the multiplicative board has an expected-draft-value reading rather than a rank product.

stage_b_transforms.formula: percentile of the raw prediction against the SAME fold's TRAINING-year prediction distribution
stage_b_transforms.fitted_on: training years of that fold only — the validation year never defines its own transform
stage_b_transforms.limitation: The training-year reference is in-sample for the fitted Stage B model, so it is mildly optimistic. Recorded rather than hidden.
stage_b_transforms.why_tested: The only transform giving a cross-class absolute scale; the other two are class-relative.

board_methods.interpretation: Calibrated-ish likelihood of being drafted. THE reference board — if Stage B does not improve on this, this is the final board.
Diagnostic benchmark only. Stage B was trained solely among drafted players and does not model draft likelihood, so it must not become the board by default.
EXPECTED DRAFT VALUE: probability of entering the draft multiplied by the conditional quality of the slot the profile resembles. This is a real expectation, not an arbitrary blend.

board_methods.signal: geometric mean of the within-board percentile ranks of Stage A and Stage B
board_methods.interpretation: Equal-principle rank fusion. Scale-free; no weights. HEURISTIC benchmark.

board_methods.signal: Stage A decile band primary, Stage B ordering within band
board_methods.interpretation: Stage A dominates; Stage B breaks ties among prospects of similar draft likelihood. Deciles are a predeclared, standard granularity — the band width was NOT tuned on validation performance.

HEURISTIC reference only. Included so the multiplicative rule can be compared against the obvious naive alternative. NOT a tuned weight — 0.5/0.5 is the single equal-weight point and no other split is evaluated.

prohibited_selection_behaviour: No blend-weight search. 0.1/0.9 ... 0.9/0.1 grids are prohibited.
No tuning of the lexicographic band width on validation performance.
No selection from a single metric.

graded_relevance.range: 0 for undrafted; (0, 1] for drafted, 1.0 at pick 1
why_this_one: Chosen BEFORE any board candidate was evaluated.
Normalises by that year's verified draft size, so a late pick in a 58-pick draft is not penalised against a 60-pick draft.
Strictly separates classes: the worst drafted prospect still scores 1/size > 0, above every undrafted prospect.
Linear in slot. No exponential 'NBA value curve' — no external source justifies one, and curvature is not tuned.
graded_relevance.IS_NOT_A_TARGET: This is an EVALUATION relevance only. It is never a training target, and it never assigns a synthetic pick to an undrafted prospect. Stage B is not trained on it.

k_definitions.k_drafted: the number of prospects actually drafted from that year's in-scope board

evaluation.low_support_note: 2025 has 2 undrafted prospects. Its BINARY metrics are unstable and must not drive selection (DEC-075). Its draft-order metrics are well posed.
selection_priority: 2. ranks high picks above low picks

score_transforms.formula: round(100 * percentile rank of the final board signal within the current class)
score_transforms.pros: simple, transparent, guaranteed monotonic, easy to explain
score_transforms.cons: class-relative — every class necessarily contains a ~100 and a ~0, so scores are not comparable across draft classes

score_transforms.formula: round(100 * percentile of the final board signal against the frozen historical DEVELOPMENT out-of-fold signal distribution)
score_transforms.pros: comparable across classes; a weak class does not manufacture a 100
score_transforms.cons: depends on a frozen reference distribution and on that distribution remaining representative
score_transforms.reference: development out-of-fold signals, 2014-2025 validation years only

score_rules.precision_note: Integer only. 92.738 implies precision the model does not have.
score_rules.monotonicity: REQUIRED: if the final board signal of A >= that of B, score(A) >= score(B). Unit-tested.
score_rules.ties: Equal signals receive equal scores. Integer rounding may also tie two distinct signals; the underlying continuous signal remains the authoritative order. Ties are NEVER broken by player name, draft outcome or any NBA information.
score_rules.semantics: A 0-100 RANKING score derived from historical pre-draft models. NOT a probability and NOT a predicted pick.

product_signals.draft_probability: Stage A P(drafted) — the ONLY output that is a probability
product_signals.draft_position_signal: Stage B conditional draft-order signal — never displayed as a literal pick (DEC-089)

stage_b_missing_policy.rule: A prospect Stage A can score must never be dropped because Stage B failed.
stage_b_missing_policy.fallback: NEUTRAL_STAGE_B — the missing prospect receives the neutral quality value (0.5 for percentile transforms, the board median for the utility transform), so the combined signal degenerates to a monotone function of Stage A alone for that prospect.
stage_b_missing_policy.rejected_alternative: Treating a missing Stage B signal as a low value. Unresolved/missing-data rows were disproportionately undrafted historically, so a penalty would turn missingness into a hidden outcome proxy.
stage_b_missing_policy.empirical_note: 0 of 617 development OOF prospects have a missing Stage B signal, so this policy is enforced by test rather than chosen by measurement.

notes: Results are not stored in this file.
Generated OOF board artifacts stay in data/interim/ml6/ and are git-ignored.
